case_name: SRL-2018 DMZ FTP Server — External Attack Perimeter
description: IIS 8.5 FTP server in DMZ (172.16.10.12). External attackers attempted malware upload and conducted coordinated credential stuffing using valid domain usernames. Server also served as DFIR response infrastructure. Attack blocked at perimeter — internal compromise used different vector.
devil_advocate: FTP server is DFIR infrastructure — legitimate tools present. Malware upload attempts were blocked and no successful compromise confirmed at this host.

artifacts.content: 2018-07-30 10:54:14 197.248.26.30 STOR /Photo.scr 550 Authorization+rules+denied+the+access | 2018-07-30 16:12:34 117.204.242.121 STOR /Photo.scr 550 Authorization+rules+denied+the+access | Two distinct IPs attempting identical malware upload via anonymous FTP
forensic_anomalies: Two geographically distinct IPs (Kenya 197.248.26.30, India 117.204.242.121) attempted to upload the same file Photo.scr — Windows screensaver executable used as malware vector
Coordinated identical attack from separate IPs indicates organized threat actor, not opportunistic scanner
Upload blocked by IIS authorization rules — attacker probing for misconfigured anonymous write access

artifacts.content: 2018-08-16: credential stuffing with valid domain usernames — USER nromanoff (218.22.253.37/CN), USER nromanoff@stark-research-labs.com (121.49.106.6/CN), USER tdungan@stark-research-labs.com (60.174.118.80/CN), USER administrator@stark-research-labs.com (200.58.160.67/BO), USER administrator (222.161.229.55/CN) — all 530 failed | 5.6MB log on Aug 16 vs avg 20KB/day
forensic_anomalies: Attacker used exact internal domain usernames (nromanoff, tdungan) — requires prior OSINT or credential leak from the organization
Same usernames appear in NROMANOFF and TDUNGAN workstation cases — confirms these are real domain accounts targeted specifically
8+ coordinated IPs across China and Bolivia in same 3-hour window — botnet or distributed attack infrastructure
Aug 16 FTP log is 280x larger than average daily log — anomalous spike indicating coordinated attack campaign

artifacts.content: srl-ftp/: Mnemosyne.sys (WinPmem memory acquisition driver) | fresponse-agent.msi (F-Response remote forensic acquisition) | sub-win-x64_base-hunt_5682_3262.exe (F-Response agent for base-hunt server) | srl-ftp/Users/rsydow-f/nxlog-4.0.3689-x64.msi | srl-ftp/Users/nfury/Asgard/
forensic_anomalies: Mnemosyne.sys and F-Response present — server was DFIR distribution point, explaining memory dump acquisition across SRL-2018 corpus
Agent filename sub-win-x64_base-hunt_5682_3262.exe links this server directly to base-hunt memory acquisition
rsydow-f (forensic analyst account) and nfury (incident responder) have personal directories — confirms DFIR team used this server during response

artifacts.content: Users present: Administrator, rsydow, rsydow-a | rsydow account hierarchy: rsydow (standard), rsydow-a (domain admin), rsydow-f (forensics) | Domain: stark-research-labs.com | rsydow-a confirmed as Domain Admin in BASE-DC registry hives
forensic_anomalies: Domain admin account rsydow-a present on DMZ-facing server — violates network segmentation principles, creates attack bridge between DMZ and internal AD
Same rsydow-a account found in DC registry as Domain Admins member — if DMZ server compromised, domain admin credentials exposed
Three-tier account structure (standard/admin/forensic) for same user suggests security-conscious organization but segmentation not enforced at DMZ boundary

artifacts.content: Multi-stage attack timeline: May 2018 server deployed | Jul 30 anonymous enumeration + Photo.scr upload attempt | Aug 16 credential stuffing peak with domain usernames | Scanning IPs: 184.105.247.194 (Shodan/ISC), 141.212.122.48 (U Michigan) | Geographic distribution: CN, KE, IN, BO, FR
forensic_anomalies: Attack progression from anonymous enumeration to targeted credential stuffing indicates attacker learned usernames between July and August 2018
Shodan and University of Michigan IPs confirm server was publicly indexed and scanned — high exposure in DMZ without proper access controls
Geographic diversity of attacking IPs (5 countries) with coordinated username knowledge suggests threat intelligence sharing or single actor with distributed infrastructure

peirce_chain.firstness: DMZ FTP server with domain admin credentials present — structural vulnerability creating implicit trust bridge
peirce_chain.secondness: Concrete attacks: Photo.scr malware upload blocked, credential stuffing with exact domain usernames from multiple IPs
peirce_chain.thirdness: Attack pattern (enumeration -> malware upload attempt -> credential stuffing with specific usernames) demonstrates persistent, intelligence-driven threat actor targeting shieldbase.lan / stark-research-labs.com

_consolidation: VIGÍA-REAL. Extracted from dmz-ftp-cdrive.E01 via ewfmount+NTFS mount in SANS SIFT. IIS FTP logs analyzed directly from Windows/System32/winevt and inetpub/logs/LogFiles/FTPSVC2/. Chain of custody maintained.
